body:
<!-- pr-reviewer: e3e7211d8f75fc07e6bfb0985a8111eab3aa2571 -->
**Not built - needs a maintainer look.** This PR adds a workflow file under `.github/` and packaging scripts (PKGBUILD runs `cargo` in `prepare/build/check`), so per review policy I read it but did not build or run anything. Reviewed at head e3e7211 (the latest commit, "ci(aur): make package validation manual").

**What looks good**
- `.github/workflows/aur-package.yml:4-5`: trigger is `workflow_dispatch` only, no push/pull_request/schedule. This matches the Actions-budget rule in AGENTS.md. It is Linux (1x billing), and each run is a full Rust build plus `cargo test`, so it should stay manual.
- Permissions are `contents: read` (line 7-8). No secrets are referenced, and nothing is pushed or published anywhere. The workflow only builds and uploads an `arch-package` artifact. The AUR publish (an SSH key, a push to aur.archlinux.org) is explicitly left as a later separate step (README, RECOMMENDED).
- PKGBUILD sources are pinned by checksum. The tag tarball sha256 `3b36cfef...66a6` matches what I got by downloading `v0.12.1.tar.gz` (hashed only, not extracted). The `.desktop` sha256 `55fc7185...4621` matches the file in the PR. `.SRCINFO` agrees with the PKGBUILD.
- The build uses `cargo fetch --locked` then `--frozen`, so dependencies are fixed by the tag's `Cargo.lock`. `LICENSE`, `TESTING.md`, `Cargo.lock` and the `assets/{posts,machines,ui,scripts,themes}` dirs all exist at `v0.12.1`, and `assets/ui/cube.png` exists.
- `aur/LICENSE` is the same MIT text as the repo root. No Autodesk/HSMWorks material or assets: the icon is the project's own `cube.png`, and the desktop file strings are original.
- Commit subjects are conventional, and the body has `Refs #72` and a `Changelog:` line.

**Local results**: not built (policy). The author reports `makepkg --printsrcinfo` matching and a successful `makepkg` in Podman; I could not confirm that.

**Requested before merge**
1. `.github/workflows/aur-package.yml` is a new workflow file, so a maintainer needs to read it. Its content looks safe to me. Things to check:
   - `actions/checkout@v4` and `actions/upload-artifact@v4` are tag-pinned, not SHA-pinned.
   - `pacman -Syu` runs in `archlinux:latest` with a rolling image, so the result is not reproducible.
   - `su builder -c "cd '$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/aur' ..."` interpolates only a workflow-provided path, not PR text.
2. The `.SRCINFO` and PKGBUILD pin `v0.12.1`, but a lot has merged since then. If the "Arch build against current main" is the goal, say so in the README. If it is meant to follow releases, the `pkgver`, tarball sha and `.SRCINFO` have to be bumped at every cut. Consider adding that to the release checklist or `scripts/release.ps1` so they do not drift. (Not blocking.)
3. `RECOMMENDED.md` (the appended `## #72: Arch Linux source package` section) is in the ledger style: heading by issue, bullets with what was chosen, why, and what was dropped. Two points: (a) it says the Flecs/LTO cause is "likely" and the fix was meant to be verified by "another Arch package build". The PR description says the user verified this, so please change the wording to state the result. (b) The new section sits under #96's last entry, which is fine for an append-only ledger, but it will probably conflict with other PRs touching the file's tail. Keep both sides on merge.
4. This PR says `Refs #72` only, which is correct: #72 asks for AUR, RPM, DEB, TAR-GZ, FreeBSD and WASM, so this does not close it.

**Questions / notes (not blocking)**
- The PKGBUILD runs the unit tests only (`--lib` on app and post), which is sensible for `check()`.
- `depends` lists runtime libs but not a GPU driver (the Vulkan ICD is the user's choice, so `vulkan-icd-loader` is the right dependency). `options=('!lto')` has an explanatory comment, good.
- The `.desktop` file has no `Keywords`/`StartupWMClass`; optional polish.
- If the maintainers later publish to the AUR, that needs an AUR SSH key as an Actions secret or a manual `git push` to aur.archlinux.org. Neither is in this PR.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
